assessment.summary: Secured the company's funding, but shareholders are behind to date
take: The raise secured the company's funding, lifting group liquidity from A$118m to A$238m and allowing Gossan Valley to continue on schedule, but it has not yet delivered a return for shareholders.

The size of the raise assumed Xantho Extended would restart in April 2026. The deferral to the December quarter, announced on 16 April, reduced the share price by 35.1% in one day. Participating holders are about 4% below the A$0.40 offer price, while holders who did not participate were diluted by 21.5% and received no value for their entitlements under the non-renounceable structure.
assessment.takeaway: Where a raise funds an operational gap, the key risk is the length of that gap, and a non-renounceable structure moves the cost of a deep discount onto holders who do not participate.

rationale: At about 27% of shares on issue, the raise was well above the 15% placement limit, and a pro-rata offer avoided the need for a shareholder vote
A pro-rata offer allowed every holder to maintain their ownership, which matters when the discount is 35.5%
The accelerated format secured most of the funds from institutions on the first day, limiting exposure to market movements
Underwriting and major shareholder commitments guaranteed the full amount despite the operational uncertainty
Non-renounceable is cheaper and quicker than renounceable, but holders who do not take up receive nothing for their entitlements

assessment.summary: Successful for the company and all shareholders
take: The placement achieved its stated purpose. Wagners issued 5.8% new equity close to the market price, and FY26 capital expenditure of A$24.4m on the concrete network and A$6.6m on composite capacity broadly matches the A$30m raised, while net debt fell from A$34.0m to A$0.8m.

Placement investors are 64% above the offer price, and holders who did not participate were diluted by only 5.8% against a 60% rise in the share price. The main limitation of this assessment is that Wagners did not set quantitative targets, so performance is measured against its stated uses of funds rather than a forecast.
assessment.takeaway: A modest placement that funds visible growth carries limited risk for both new and existing investors.

rationale: Speed and certainty, as the full A$30m was committed before the market was told, with minimal exposure to price movements
At about 6% of shares on issue, the raise fitted within existing placement capacity
Institutional demand allowed pricing close to market, limiting the cost to existing holders
Retail holders were excluded, although the impact was limited by the small size of the raise

assessment.summary: Successful for the company's launch, but not for placement investors
take: EBR met every target set at the raise, with first US sales in 2025, 87 implants across 29 US hospitals in the first half of 2026 and cash sufficient to fund operations into late 2026. Investors who subscribed at A$1.00 are nonetheless 73.5% below their entry price.

The raise was sized to fund the business into late 2026, well before it could become self-funding, so EBR raised a further A$150m at A$0.38 in June 2026 and continued to report substantial doubt about its ability to continue as a going concern in its June 2026 10-Q. The timing of the 2025 raise was still favourable for the company, as it secured capital at a far higher price than was available in 2026.
assessment.takeaway: For a pre-revenue company, the funding runway effectively sets the date of the next raise, so meeting launch milestones does not protect investors from further dilution.

rationale: Raising immediately after FDA approval took advantage of investor interest and the higher share price that followed the approval
A placement was the fastest way to fund the US launch before revenue started
Settlement underwriting gave certainty of funds once the bookbuild closed
The SPP let retail holders participate on similar terms, offsetting their exclusion from the placement
